title: Astroscale debris removal
summary: Rendezvous and inspection of defunct spacecraft as a precursor to removal.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Astroscale's ADRAS-J mission in 2024 approached and inspected a spent Japanese upper stage, demonstrating the navigation needed to match a tumbling object in orbit. Removal requires a docking or capture mechanism and a customer willing to pay for a public good. Insurers and regulators, not satellite operators, are the likely funders.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Proof of concept
Estimated window 2024–2030
Confidence label Researching
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Debris is a commons problem: the economics only work when a regulator, insurer or treaty makes someone pay.

What Would Change The View

  • Government service contracts.
  • Capture technology demonstrations.
  • Insurance pricing for collision risk.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
